name: BitLuso Pay
author: BitLuso

sections.description:
BitLuso Pay lets your WooCommerce store accept Bitcoin payments, on-chain and over Lightning.

At checkout, the customer chooses BitLuso Pay, pays on a payment page hosted by BitLuso, and returns
to your order confirmation. Payments go directly from the customer’s wallet to your own wallet.

BitLuso is non-custodial software: it never holds, converts or transfers your funds, and it has no
access to your wallet’s private keys.

A BitLuso merchant account is required.

Order status

Orders are updated automatically when a payment is detected on the Bitcoin network, through a signed
callback to your store, not when the customer returns to your site. Confirmed payments complete the
order and send your usual WooCommerce emails. Late or partial payments are put on hold with a note
for you to review. Before completing an order, the plugin checks that the amount and currency match.

Setup

Paste the API key and API secret from your BitLuso dashboard into
WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → BitLuso Pay, and save. Saving verifies your credentials and
registers your store with BitLuso automatically.

External services

This plugin connects to the BitLuso Portal (https://bitluso.pt). The Portal hosts the payment page
and detects payments on the Bitcoin network. Your site contacts https://portal.bitluso.pt only in
these three cases:

  1. When you save the settings with the gateway enabled: your API key and your store’s callback URL
    are sent to verify the credentials. Nothing is sent while the gateway is disabled or on
    activation.
  2. When a customer chooses BitLuso Pay at checkout.
  3. When a payment is detected: BitLuso calls your site back with a signed request, which is rejected
    if the signature, timestamp or order key does not match.

The payment page is hosted on portal.bitluso.pt. No analytics or usage data is collected, and the
plugin does not contact any other service.

Using this plugin means all of that is handled under BitLuso’s terms of use and privacy policy
(both in Portuguese):

  • Terms of use: https://bitluso.pt/termos/
  • Privacy policy: https://bitluso.pt/privacidade/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce 8.0 or newer must be active.
  2. Create an API key in your BitLuso dashboard, under Integrações → WooCommerce. The secret is
    shown only once.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → BitLuso Pay, paste the API key and API secret, tick
    Enable BitLuso Pay and save.
  4. Saving verifies the credentials and registers the callback URL. A confirmation notice tells you
    whether you are connected in live or test mode.

Your shop must be reachable over HTTPS from the public internet, or BitLuso cannot report payments
back to it. A shop on localhost will take payments but never complete the orders.
sections.faq:
Do I need a BitLuso account?

Yes. The plugin is a client for the BitLuso payment service; it does nothing on its own. See the
External services section above.

Which coins can my customers pay with?

Whatever your BitLuso store has enabled — on-chain Bitcoin, Lightning, or both.
sections.changelog:
1.3.1

  • The checkout now reads “Bitcoin & Lightning via” followed by the BitLuso Pay logo, in both the block and the classic checkout, instead of showing the old button image.
  • Rewrote the plugin description and the External services section, and shortened the FAQ.

1.3.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Updates now come from WordPress.org; the plugin no longer checks the BitLuso portal for new versions.
  • Uninstalling the plugin now deletes its settings, including the stored API credentials.
  • Hardened the callback listener: request headers and the values BitLuso reports are sanitized before use.

1.2.0

  • Removed the Title, Description and portal URL settings. The checkout shows the BitLuso button, and the portal URL is now a constant that wp-config.php can override.
  • The callback signing secret is issued by BitLuso when the shop registers its callback URL, instead of being pasted in by hand.

1.1.0

  • Cart and Checkout blocks support, and High-Performance Order Storage compatibility.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: hosted Bitcoin and Lightning checkout for WooCommerce.
